title: Networks
subtitle: From social networking to neural pathways to the increasingly networked structure of the economy, complex networks are an integral part of our lives. NECSI research on the structure and dynamics of networks expands our understanding of how biological, social, and technological networks behave.

## Network Modeling

### NECSI researchers developed general models describing how networked systems respond to disturbances.

David D. Chinellato, Irving R. Epstein, Dan Braha, Yaneer Bar-Yam, and Marcus A.M. de Aguiar, [**Dynamical response of networks under external perturbations: Exact results**](/dynamical-response-of-networks-under-external-perturbations), *Journal of Statistical Physics* 159: 221–230 (2015).

Marcus A.M. de Aguiar and Yaneer Bar-Yam, [**Spectral analysis and the dynamic response of complex networks**](/spectral-analysis-and-the-dynamic-response-of-complex-networks), *Physical Review E* 71: 016106 (2005).

## Biological

### By describing the way regulatory networks behave we can describe the functioning of cells.

Benjamin de Bivort, Sui Huang, and Y. Bar-Yam, [**Dynamics of cellular level function and regulation derived from murine expression array data**](/dynamics-of-cellular-level-function-and-regulation-derived-from-murine-expression-array-data), *PNAS* 101(51): 17687-17692 (2004).

Yaneer Bar-Yam, [**Sleep as temporary brain dissociation**](/sleep-as-temporary-brain-dissociation), *CSDL Research Report YB-0005-10.10.92* (1993).
